questions.question: What does "fluency" mean when speaking English?
options: Speaking smoothly and naturally, even if you make some mistakes
Speaking without ever making a single mistake
Speaking as fast as possible
Knowing every word in the dictionary
questions.explanation: Fluency is about communicating smoothly so the conversation flows naturally. Even native speakers make mistakes.

questions.question: What is "paraphrasing"?
options: Saying something in other words, for example when you forget a specific word
Repeating exactly what someone else said
Reading aloud from a script
Speaking very slowly
questions.explanation: Paraphrasing means expressing something with different words, like saying "I am very, very hungry" instead of "I am famished".

questions.question: In a presentation, roughly how much time should the body (the main part) take?
options: About 80 %
About 50 %
About 10 %
About 30 %
questions.explanation: A presentation is usually about 10 % introduction, 80 % body and 10 % conclusion.

questions.question: Which of these is a recommended way to deal with nervousness before a presentation?
options: Practise many times and use cue cards instead of reading a full script
Write down every word and read it from the paper
Avoid looking at the audience completely
Speak as quickly as possible to finish early
questions.explanation: Practising several times, breathing deeply, looking at friendly faces and using cue cards are all good strategies against nervousness.

questions.question: You don't understand what someone just said in a conversation. What is a good thing to say?
options: "Sorry, could you say that again, please?"
"That is wrong."
Nothing - just nod and pretend you understood
"I speak Norwegian."
questions.explanation: Asking someone politely to repeat or explain is an important communication strategy that keeps the conversation going.
